records.source: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν μεγάλην, καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐφωτίσθη ἐκ τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: After these things I saw another angel coming down out of the heaven, having authority great, and the earth was lit up from the glory of him.
pieces: After this I saw another angel coming down from heaven. He had great authority, and the earth shone with his glory.

L.1: After these things I saw another angel coming down from heaven, having great authority, and the earth was lit up by his glory.

R.1: Then I saw another angel coming down from heaven. He had great power. His glory was so bright that it lit up the whole earth.

decisions.choice: the earth lit by his glory: Ezekiel 43:2
decisions.reason: When God's glory returned to the temple, "the earth shone with his glory" (Ezekiel 43:2). The angel comes from God's presence and reflects his brightness.

records.heading: The fall of Babylon

records.source: καὶ ἔκραξεν ἐν ἰσχυρᾷ φωνῇ λέγων· Ἔπεσεν, ἔπεσεν Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, καὶ ἐγένετο κατοικητήριον δαιμονίων καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς πνεύματος ἀκαθάρτου καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς ὀρνέου ἀκαθάρτου καὶ φυλακὴ παντὸς θηρίου ἀκαθάρτου καὶ μεμισημένου, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς πέπτωκαν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς μετ’ αὐτῆς ἐπόρνευσαν, καὶ οἱ ἔμποροι τῆς γῆς ἐκ τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ στρήνους αὐτῆς ἐπλούτησαν.
records.gloss: And he cried out in mighty voice saying: Fell, fell Babylon the great, and became a dwelling of demons and a prison of every spirit unclean and a prison of every bird unclean and a prison of every beast unclean and having been hated, \v 3 because of the wine of the passion of the immorality of her have fallen all the nations, and the kings of the earth with her committed immorality, and the merchants of the earth from the power of the luxury of her became rich.
pieces: He shouted with a mighty voice: "Babylon the great has fallen, has fallen! She has become a home for demons, a lair for every unclean spirit, a lair for every unclean bird, a lair for every unclean and hateful beast.
Through the wine of her raging immorality all the nations have fallen; the kings of the earth committed immorality with her, and the earth's merchants grew rich from her extravagant luxury."

L.2: And he cried out with a mighty voice, saying, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great! She has become a dwelling place of demons and a haunt of every unclean spirit and a haunt of every unclean bird and a haunt of every unclean and hated beast,
L.3: for all the nations have fallen by the wine of the passion of her sexual immorality, and the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality with her, and the merchants of the earth grew rich from the power of her luxury."

R.2: He shouted with a powerful voice, "Babylon the great city has fallen! It has fallen! Now it is a home for demons and for every kind of evil spirit. It is a place where unclean birds and hated animals live.
R.3: All the nations fell because they drank the wine of her sexual sins. The kings of the earth committed sexual sins with her. The merchants of the earth became rich because she spent so much on luxuries."

decisions.choice: a ruin haunted by wild creatures: the prophets on Babylon and Edom
decisions.reason: The cry "Fallen, fallen is Babylon" is Isaiah's (21:9; compare 14:8). The prophets describe fallen Babylon and Edom as ruins where jackals, owls and wild goats live and demons haunt (Isaiah 13:19-22; 34:11-15; Jeremiah 50:39; 51:37). φυλακὴ means a prison or guarded place: the city becomes the haunt of everything unclean.

decisions.choice: have fallen
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads πέπτωκαν, "have fallen": the nations have fallen through the wine of her immorality. Many manuscripts have a word that differs by a letter and means "have drunk" (compare 14:8; 17:2). The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: luxury: extravagance and arrogance
decisions.reason: στρήνους means excessive luxury, with the insolence that goes with it. Her wealth made the merchants rich (18:11-19).

decisions.choice: haunt (L); lair (B); a place where ... live (R)
decisions.reason: The word means a guarded place; "haunt" and "lair" say what it is in a ruined city (m1).

records.source: Καὶ ἤκουσα ἄλλην φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λέγουσαν· Ἐξέλθατε, ὁ λαός μου, ἐξ αὐτῆς, ἵνα μὴ συγκοινωνήσητε ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐκ τῶν πληγῶν αὐτῆς ἵνα μὴ λάβητε·
records.gloss: And I heard another voice out of the heaven saying: Come out, the people of me, out of her, so that not you share in the sins of her, and out of the plagues of her that not you receive,
pieces: Then I heard another voice from heaven: "Leave her, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, so that you have no part in her sins and do not suffer any of her plagues.

L.4: And I heard another voice from heaven saying, "Come out of her, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, so that you do not share in her sins, and so that you do not receive any of her plagues,

R.4: Then I heard another voice from heaven. It said, "My people, come out of that city! Then you will not join in her sins, and you will not suffer from her plagues.

decisions.choice: Come out of her, my people: the call to leave Babylon
decisions.reason: The prophets called God's people to flee Babylon before its fall (Jeremiah 50:8; 51:6, 45; Isaiah 48:20; 52:11), and Paul applies the words to believers' separation from idolatry (2 Corinthians 6:17). The call is less about moving house than about refusing to share in the city's sins.

decisions.choice: my people: the speaker is God or Christ
decisions.reason: The voice speaks of "my people", so it is God's or Christ's. It continues to the end of 18:8.

decisions.choice: my: deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The speaker is God or Christ (m2).

records.heading: Come out of her, my people

records.source: ὅτι ἐκολλήθησαν αὐτῆς αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ἄχρι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἐμνημόνευσεν ὁ θεὸς τὰ ἀδικήματα αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: because were heaped up of her the sins as far as the heaven, and remembered the God the crimes of her.
pieces: For her sins have stacked up as high as heaven, and God has not forgotten her crimes.

L.5: for her sins have piled up as far as heaven, and God has remembered her crimes.

R.5: Her sins are piled up as high as the sky. God remembers all the wrong things she has done.

decisions.choice: sins piled to heaven: Jeremiah 51:9
decisions.reason: "Her judgment has reached up to heaven" (Jeremiah 51:9; compare Genesis 18:20-21, the outcry against Sodom). ἐκολλήθησαν means stuck together, heaped up. God remembers in order to judge (16:19).

records.source: ἀπόδοτε αὐτῇ ὡς καὶ αὐτὴ ἀπέδωκεν, καὶ διπλώσατε τὰ διπλᾶ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῆς· ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ ᾧ ἐκέρασεν κεράσατε αὐτῇ διπλοῦν·
records.gloss: Give back to her as also she gave back, and double the double according to the works of her; in the cup in which she mixed, mix for her double.
pieces: Treat her as she treated others; repay her twice over for her deeds; mix her a double draught in the very cup she mixed.

L.6: Pay her back as she herself paid back, and repay [her] double according to her works; in the cup that she mixed, mix double for her.

R.6: Do to her what she did to others. Pay her back twice as much for what she has done. She mixed a drink of suffering for others. Now mix her a drink twice as strong.

decisions.choice: double: full repayment
alternatives: literally twice the harm she did
decisions.reason: In the prophets "double" can mean a full and fitting measure (Jeremiah 16:18; Isaiah 40:2). The point is that her judgment matches her deeds completely, as 18:7 says: "as much as she glorified herself".

decisions.choice: addressed to the agents of judgment
decisions.reason: The commands are most likely addressed to those who carry out God's judgment, such as the angels or the beast and the ten horns (17:16). God's people are told to leave the city (18:4), not to take revenge (Romans 12:19).

records.source: ὅσα ἐδόξασεν αὑτὴν καὶ ἐστρηνίασεν, τοσοῦτον δότε αὐτῇ βασανισμὸν καὶ πένθος.
records.gloss: As much as she glorified herself and lived in luxury, so much give to her torment and grief.
pieces: In proportion to the glory she gave herself and the luxury she lived in, give her torment and mourning.

L.7: As much as she glorified herself and lived in luxury, so much torment and grief give her.

R.7: She gave herself glory and lived in luxury. Now give her the same amount of pain and sorrow.

decisions.choice: the measure of her pride is the measure of her judgment
decisions.reason: She claimed the glory that belongs to God (compare 14:7; 15:4). Her judgment matches her self-exaltation.

records.source: ὅτι ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῆς λέγει ὅτι Κάθημαι βασίλισσα, καὶ χήρα οὐκ εἰμί, καὶ πένθος οὐ μὴ ἴδω.
records.gloss: because in the heart of her she says: I sit a queen and a widow not I am, and grief not not I see.
pieces: In her heart she keeps saying, 'Here I sit, a queen; I am not a widow, and mourning I will never see.'

L.7: For in her heart she says, 'I sit as a queen, and I am not a widow, and I will never see grief.'

R.7: She says to herself, 'I am a queen sitting on my throne. I am not a widow. I will never be sad.'

decisions.choice: I sit as queen and am no widow: Isaiah 47
decisions.reason: Babylon said, "I shall be mistress forever ... I shall not sit as a widow or know the loss of children", and God replied that both would come on her in a moment, in one day (Isaiah 47:7-9; compare Zephaniah 2:15). John uses the same boast and the same answer (18:8).

records.source: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν μιᾷ ἡμέρᾳ ἥξουσιν αἱ πληγαὶ αὐτῆς, θάνατος καὶ πένθος καὶ λιμός, καὶ ἐν πυρὶ κατακαυθήσεται· ὅτι ἰσχυρὸς κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὁ κρίνας αὐτήν.
records.gloss: Because of this in one day will come the plagues of her, death and grief and famine, and with fire she will be burned up, because mighty Lord the God the [one] having judged her.
pieces: So her plagues will strike in one day, death, grief, and famine, and fire will burn her up; for the Lord God who has judged her is strong."

L.8: Therefore in one day her plagues will come, death and grief and famine, and she will be burned up with fire, for mighty is the Lord God who has judged her."

R.8: So in one day terrible things will happen to her: death, sadness, and hunger. She will be burned up with fire. The Lord God who judges her is powerful."

decisions.choice: in one day: the sudden fall of Isaiah 47:9
decisions.reason: See the note on 18:7. The judgment is sudden: in one day, and in one hour (18:10, 17, 19). The fire was foretold in 17:16.

records.source: Καὶ κλαύσουσιν καὶ κόψονται ἐπ’ αὐτὴν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς οἱ μετ’ αὐτῆς πορνεύσαντες καὶ στρηνιάσαντες, ὅταν βλέπωσιν τὸν καπνὸν τῆς πυρώσεως αὐτῆς, ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἑστηκότες διὰ τὸν φόβον τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῆς λέγοντες· Οὐαὶ οὐαί, ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, Βαβυλὼν ἡ πόλις ἡ ἰσχυρά, ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἦλθεν ἡ κρίσις σου.
records.gloss: And will weep and wail over her the kings of the earth, those with her having committed immorality and lived in luxury, when they see the smoke of the burning of her, \v 10 from afar standing because of the fear of the torment of her, saying: Woe woe, the city the great, Babylon the city the strong, because in one hour came the judgment of you.
pieces: The earth's kings, who shared her immorality and her luxury, will weep and beat their breasts over her as they watch the smoke rise from her burning.
Keeping far away for fear of her torment, they will say, "Woe, woe, great city, Babylon, city of strength! In a single hour your judgment has come."

L.9: And the kings of the earth who committed sexual immorality and lived in luxury with her will weep and wail over her when they see the smoke of her burning,
L.10: standing far off because of the fear of her torment, saying, "Woe, woe, the great city, Babylon, the strong city, for in one hour your judgment has come!"

R.9: The kings of the earth committed sexual sins with her and enjoyed her riches. When they see the smoke from her burning, they will cry and be very sad.
R.10: They will be afraid of her suffering, so they will stand far away. They will say, "How terrible! How terrible for you, great city, powerful city of Babylon! In just one hour your punishment has come!"

decisions.choice: the laments over Tyre in Ezekiel 26-27
decisions.reason: The laments of kings, merchants and sailors follow Ezekiel's laments over Tyre, the great trading city, whose fall the princes of the coast, the merchants and the seamen mourned from a distance (Ezekiel 26:15-18; 27:28-36). Babylon's mourners grieve for their own losses more than for her.

decisions.choice: in one hour: suddenly
decisions.reason: The phrase is repeated in each lament (18:10, 17, 19): a city that seemed permanent is gone in a moment.

decisions.choice: Woe (L, B); How terrible (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:13.

records.source: Καὶ οἱ ἔμποροι τῆς γῆς κλαίουσιν καὶ πενθοῦσιν ἐπ’ αὐτήν, ὅτι τὸν γόμον αὐτῶν οὐδεὶς ἀγοράζει οὐκέτι, γόμον χρυσοῦ καὶ ἀργύρου καὶ λίθου τιμίου καὶ μαργαριτῶν καὶ βυσσίνου καὶ πορφύρας καὶ σιρικοῦ καὶ κοκκίνου, καὶ πᾶν ξύλον θύϊνον καὶ πᾶν σκεῦος ἐλεφάντινον καὶ πᾶν σκεῦος ἐκ ξύλου τιμιωτάτου καὶ χαλκοῦ καὶ σιδήρου καὶ μαρμάρου, καὶ κιννάμωμον καὶ ἄμωμον καὶ θυμιάματα καὶ μύρον καὶ λίβανον καὶ οἶνον καὶ ἔλαιον καὶ σεμίδαλιν καὶ σῖτον καὶ κτήνη καὶ πρόβατα, καὶ ἵππων καὶ ῥεδῶν καὶ σωμάτων, καὶ ψυχὰς ἀνθρώπων.
records.gloss: And the merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, because the cargo of them no one buys any longer, \v 12 cargo of gold and of silver and of stone precious and of pearls and of fine linen and of purple and of silk and of scarlet, and all wood citron and every article of ivory and every article out of wood most precious and of bronze and of iron and of marble, \v 13 and cinnamon and spice and incenses and myrrh and frankincense and wine and oil and fine flour and wheat and cattle and sheep, and of horses and of carriages and of bodies, and souls of men.
pieces: The merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, because no one buys their goods any more:
goods of gold, silver, precious stones, and pearls; fine linen, purple, silk, and scarlet; all kinds of citron wood, and all sorts of objects of ivory, costly wood, bronze, iron, and marble;
cinnamon and spice, incense, myrrh, and frankincense; wine and olive oil, fine flour and wheat; cattle and sheep; horses and carriages; and slaves, human lives.

L.11: And the merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, because no one buys their cargo anymore,
L.12: cargo of gold and silver and precious stone and pearls and fine linen and purple and silk and scarlet, and all citron wood and every article of ivory and every article of most precious wood and bronze and iron and marble,
L.13: and cinnamon and spice and incense and myrrh and frankincense and wine and olive oil and fine flour and wheat and cattle and sheep, and of horses and of carriages, and of bodies, and souls of {{gender:human beings|men}}.

R.11: The merchants of the earth will cry and be sad about her, because no one buys their goods anymore.
R.12: They sold gold, silver, jewels, and pearls. They sold fine linen, purple cloth, silk, and red cloth. They sold sweet-smelling wood and things made of ivory, expensive wood, bronze, iron, and marble.
R.13: They sold cinnamon, spices, incense, myrrh, and frankincense. They sold wine, olive oil, flour, and wheat. They sold cattle, sheep, horses, and carriages. They even sold people as slaves.

decisions.choice: the cargo list: Ezekiel 27
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 27:12-24 lists the goods that Tyre traded with every nation, ending with slaves (27:13). Here the list of luxuries that flowed into the great city ends the same way.

decisions.choice: citron wood: a costly, scented wood
decisions.reason: Citron wood from North Africa was prized in Rome for its grain and scent, and tables made from it were famously expensive.

decisions.choice: bodies, and souls of human beings: the slave trade
decisions.reason: σωμάτων, "bodies", was a common term for slaves in the market. "Souls of human beings" may explain it or add to it: what the city bought and sold included people's very lives. The list ends with its worst item.

decisions.choice: bodies, and souls of human beings (L); slaves, human lives (B); people as slaves (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek words; Balanced and Readable say what they meant (m3). "Slaves" stays at every level, as the style guide keeps it for people bought and sold.

records.source: καὶ ἡ ὀπώρα σου τῆς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ψυχῆς ἀπῆλθεν ἀπὸ σοῦ, καὶ πάντα τὰ λιπαρὰ καὶ τὰ λαμπρὰ ἀπώλετο ἀπὸ σοῦ, καὶ οὐκέτι οὐ μὴ αὐτὰ εὑρήσουσιν.
records.gloss: And the ripe fruit of you of the desire of the soul went away from you, and all the rich things and the splendid things perished from you, and no longer not not them they will find.
pieces: The harvest of all that your heart desired has left you, and everything rich and dazzling is lost to you; no one will ever find it again.

L.14: And the ripe fruit of your soul's desire has gone from you, and all the rich and splendid things have perished from you, and never again will they find them.

R.14: Babylon, the good things you wanted so much are gone. All your riches and beautiful things have disappeared. No one will ever find them again.

decisions.choice: a sudden address to the city
decisions.reason: The account turns and speaks to the city directly, as in 18:22-23. "They will find" is impersonal: no one will find them.

decisions.choice: Babylon (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the city being addressed.

records.source: οἱ ἔμποροι τούτων, οἱ πλουτήσαντες ἀπ’ αὐτῆς, ἀπὸ μακρόθεν στήσονται διὰ τὸν φόβον τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῆς κλαίοντες καὶ πενθοῦντες, λέγοντες· Οὐαὶ οὐαί, ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, ἡ περιβεβλημένη βύσσινον καὶ πορφυροῦν καὶ κόκκινον καὶ κεχρυσωμένη χρυσίῳ καὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ καὶ μαργαρίτῃ, ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἠρημώθη ὁ τοσοῦτος πλοῦτος.
records.gloss: The merchants of these things, the [ones] having become rich from her, from afar will stand because of the fear of the torment of her, weeping and mourning, \v 16 saying: Woe woe, the city the great, the [one] having been clothed in fine linen and purple and scarlet, and having been gilded with gold and stone precious and pearl, \v 17 because in one hour was laid waste the so great wealth.
pieces: Those who dealt in these things and were made rich by her will keep their distance in fear of her torment, weeping and grieving:
"Woe, woe for the great city, which wore fine linen, purple, and scarlet, and was decked with gold, jewels, and pearls!
So much wealth, and in one hour it is ruined!"

L.15: The merchants of these things, who grew rich from her, will stand far off because of the fear of her torment, weeping and mourning,
L.16: saying, "Woe, woe, the great city, clothed in fine linen and purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold and precious stone and pearl,
L.17: for in one hour such great wealth has been laid waste!"

R.15: The merchants who became rich by selling these things to her will stand far away. They will be afraid of her suffering. They will cry and be sad.
R.16: They will say, "How terrible! How terrible for the great city! She dressed in fine linen, purple, and red clothes. She wore gold, jewels, and pearls.
R.17: In just one hour all her riches are gone!"

decisions.choice: the laments over Tyre in Ezekiel 26-27
decisions.reason: The laments of kings, merchants and sailors follow Ezekiel's laments over Tyre, the great trading city, whose fall the princes of the coast, the merchants and the seamen mourned from a distance (Ezekiel 26:15-18; 27:28-36). Babylon's mourners grieve for their own losses more than for her.

decisions.choice: her clothing: the prostitute of 17:4
decisions.reason: The city is described in the words used of the woman in 17:4: the city and the prostitute are one.

records.source: Καὶ πᾶς κυβερνήτης καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἐπὶ τόπον πλέων, καὶ ναῦται καὶ ὅσοι τὴν θάλασσαν ἐργάζονται, ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔστησαν καὶ ἔκραξαν βλέποντες τὸν καπνὸν τῆς πυρώσεως αὐτῆς λέγοντες· Τίς ὁμοία τῇ πόλει τῇ μεγάλῃ;
records.gloss: And every helmsman and every one the to a place sailing and sailors and as many as the sea work, from afar stood \v 18 and cried out seeing the smoke of the burning of her, saying: What like to the city the great?
pieces: Every helmsman, every traveler by sea, the sailors and all who work on the sea kept their distance
and shouted as they looked at the smoke of her burning: "What city was like the great city?"

L.17: And every ship's captain and everyone who sails to any place, and sailors, and all who work the sea, stood far off
L.18: and cried out as they saw the smoke of her burning, saying, "What [city] is like the great city?"

R.17: Every ship captain, every passenger, every sailor, and everyone who earns a living on the sea stood far away.
R.18: They saw the smoke from her burning and shouted, "There was never a city as great as this one!"

decisions.choice: the seamen's lament: Ezekiel 27:28-32
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel the pilots and sailors stand on the shore, cry out bitterly, throw dust on their heads, and ask, "Who is like Tyre?" (Ezekiel 27:28-32). The question here echoes the world's praise of the beast (13:4).

decisions.choice: a statement (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the rhetorical question.

records.source: καὶ ἔβαλον χοῦν ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ ἔκραξαν κλαίοντες καὶ πενθοῦντες λέγοντες· Οὐαὶ οὐαί, ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, ἐν ᾗ ἐπλούτησαν πάντες οἱ ἔχοντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ ἐκ τῆς τιμιότητος αὐτῆς, ὅτι μιᾷ ὥρᾳ ἠρημώθη.
records.gloss: And they threw dust on the heads of them and cried out weeping and mourning, saying: Woe woe, the city the great, in which became rich all those having the ships in the sea from the wealth of her, because in one hour she was laid waste.
pieces: Throwing dust on their heads, weeping and mourning, they cried: "Woe, woe for the great city! Her wealth made rich everyone who owned a ship at sea, and in one hour she has been laid waste."

L.19: And they threw dust on their heads and cried out, weeping and mourning, saying, "Woe, woe, the great city, in which all who had ships on the sea grew rich from her wealth, for in one hour she has been laid waste!"

R.19: They threw dust on their heads to show their sorrow. They cried and shouted, "How terrible! How terrible for the great city! Everyone who owned ships became rich because of her riches. But in just one hour she has been destroyed!"

decisions.choice: dust on the head: a sign of mourning
decisions.reason: Throwing dust on one's head was a sign of grief and humiliation (Joshua 7:6; Ezekiel 27:30).

records.source: Εὐφραίνου ἐπ’ αὐτῇ, οὐρανέ, καὶ οἱ ἅγιοι καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ προφῆται, ὅτι ἔκρινεν ὁ θεὸς τὸ κρίμα ὑμῶν ἐξ αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: Rejoice over her, heaven, and the saints and the apostles and the prophets, because judged the God the judgment of you out of her.
pieces: Celebrate her fall, heaven, and you holy people, apostles, and prophets! God has taken up your case against her and judged it.

L.20: Rejoice over her, heaven, and [you] saints and apostles and prophets, for God has judged your case against her!

R.20: Heaven, be happy because of what happened to her! God's people, apostles, and prophets, be happy! God has punished her for what she did to you.

decisions.choice: God has judged your case against her
alternatives: God has turned on her the judgment she passed on you
decisions.reason: "Judged your judgment from her" is an unusual phrase. It most likely means that God has given judgment in favor of his people against the city that condemned them, answering the martyrs' cry for justice (6:10; 19:2). It may also mean that the sentence she passed on them now falls on her.

decisions.choice: joy at God's justice, not at suffering
decisions.reason: Heaven rejoices that God has vindicated his people and ended the city's oppression (19:1-3). The call contrasts with the self-pity of those who shared her sins (18:9-19).

decisions.choice: saints (L); holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

records.source: Καὶ ἦρεν εἷς ἄγγελος ἰσχυρὸς λίθον ὡς μύλινον μέγαν, καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν λέγων· Οὕτως ὁρμήματι βληθήσεται Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη πόλις, καὶ οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἔτι.
records.gloss: And took up one angel mighty a stone like a millstone great and threw into the sea, saying: Thus with violence will be thrown Babylon the great city, and not not will be found any longer.
pieces: A strong angel picked up a stone like a huge millstone and flung it into the sea. "Like this," he said, "violently, Babylon the great city will be hurled down, and no one will find her any more.

L.21: And a mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone and threw [it] into the sea, saying, "Thus with violence Babylon the great city will be thrown down, and will never be found again.

R.21: Then a powerful angel picked up a large stone, as big as a millstone for grinding grain. He threw it into the sea and said, "That is how the great city of Babylon will be thrown down. No one will ever see it again.

decisions.choice: a stone thrown into the sea: Jeremiah 51:63-64
decisions.reason: Jeremiah told Seraiah to tie a stone to the scroll of Babylon's doom and throw it into the Euphrates, saying, "Thus shall Babylon sink, to rise no more" (Jeremiah 51:63-64). A millstone was a large, heavy stone, sometimes turned by a donkey (compare Mark 9:42).

decisions.choice: the angel's words run to 18:24
decisions.reason: The angel speaks to the end of the chapter, addressing the city as "you" in 18:22-23.

records.source: καὶ φωνὴ κιθαρῳδῶν καὶ μουσικῶν καὶ αὐλητῶν καὶ σαλπιστῶν οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ πᾶς τεχνίτης πάσης τέχνης οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ φωνὴ μύλου οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ φῶς λύχνου οὐ μὴ φάνῃ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι, καὶ φωνὴ νυμφίου καὶ νύμφης οὐ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐν σοὶ ἔτι· ὅτι οἱ ἔμποροί σου ἦσαν οἱ μεγιστᾶνες τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἐν τῇ φαρμακείᾳ σου ἐπλανήθησαν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἐν αὐτῇ αἷμα προφητῶν καὶ ἁγίων εὑρέθη καὶ πάντων τῶν ἐσφαγμένων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
records.gloss: And sound of harpists and musicians and flute players and trumpeters not not will be heard in you any longer, and every craftsman of every craft not not will be found in you any longer, and sound of millstone not not will be heard in you any longer, \v 23 and light of lamp not not will shine in you any longer, and voice of bridegroom and bride not not will be heard in you any longer; because the merchants of you were the great ones of the earth, because by the sorcery of you were deceived all the nations, \v 24 and in her blood of prophets and of saints was found and of all those having been slaughtered on the earth.
pieces: No more will the music of harpists and singers, of flute players and trumpeters, be heard in you; no craftsman of any trade will be found in you again; the sound of the millstone will be heard in you no more;

the light of a lamp will shine in you no more; the voices of bridegroom and bride will be heard in you no more. For your merchants were the great ones of the earth, and by your sorcery all the nations were led astray.
The blood of prophets and of God's holy people was found in her, the blood of all who have been slaughtered on the earth."

L.22: And the sound of harpists and musicians and flute players and trumpeters will never be heard in you again, and no craftsman of any craft will ever be found in you again, and the sound of a millstone will never be heard in you again,
L.23: and the light of a lamp will never shine in you again, and the voice of bridegroom and bride will never be heard in you again; for your merchants were the great ones of the earth, for by your sorcery all the nations were deceived,
L.24: and in her was found the blood of prophets and of saints and of all who have been slaughtered on the earth."

R.22: No one will ever play music in you again, on harps, flutes, or trumpets. No one will ever work at any trade in you again. No one will ever grind grain in you again.
R.23: No lamp will ever shine in you again. No one will ever celebrate a wedding in you again. Your merchants were the most important people in the world, and you fooled all the nations with your magic.
R.24: The blood of the prophets and of God's people was found in that city, and the blood of everyone who was killed on the earth."

decisions.choice: the silence of a dead city: Jeremiah 25:10
decisions.reason: "I will banish from them the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp" (Jeremiah 25:10; compare 7:34; 16:9). Every sign of ordinary life, work, music and marriage, is gone.

decisions.choice: merchants who were princes: Tyre
decisions.reason: Isaiah 23:8 says of Tyre that "her merchants were princes". The city's wealth made traders into the world's great ones.

decisions.choice: sorcery: deception that bewitched the nations
decisions.reason: φαρμακείᾳ is magic or sorcery (9:21). Here it describes the city's seductive power, by which it led the nations astray.

decisions.choice: the blood of all who were slaughtered on the earth
decisions.reason: The city is held responsible for the blood of the prophets and saints, and of all who have been killed on the earth, as Jesus said of Jerusalem's leaders (Matthew 23:35). The city stands for the whole order of the world that sheds innocent blood. The address turns from "you" to "her" in this last sentence.

decisions.choice: saints (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.
